title: Suppose k runners having distinct constant speeds start at a common point and run laps on a unit length circular track
exact_target: Does every runner eventually have circular distance at least the reciprocal of the number of runners from every other runner?

sources.citation: ULAM.AI and the UnsolvedMath Contributors, \emph{UnsolvedMath: A Curated Collection of Open Mathematics Problems}, record 3100057 (AMR-030-0057). CC BY 4.0.
J. Barajas and O. Serra, \emph{The lonely runner with seven runners} (2007), Abstract and Section1, geometric Lonely Runner Conjecture and nearest-integer reformulation, pages1--2.
